key_insight: A Partially-Averaged Navier-Stokes (PANS) model can reproduce the curvature-driven turbulence behavior in annular Poiseuille flow with accuracy comparable to DNS and other scale-resolving RANS-based methods.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a lower-cost option for predicting turbulent flow in curved annular passages relevant to heat exchangers and similar engineering systems.
method: Simulated turbulent annular Poiseuille flow at Re_Dh = 8900.
Used the PANS variable-resolution turbulence framework built on conventional RANS modeling.
Assessed the influence of inner-wall transverse curvature via the radius ratio η = Ri/Ro.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the PANS results capture transverse wall curvature effects comparably to DNS and other RANS-based scale-resolving approaches.
watch_item: Performance may depend on model resolution settings and careful calibration, so the reduced-cost advantage should be validated for other geometries and Reynolds numbers.
paper_title: Partially-Averaged Navier-Stokes simulation of turbulent annular Poiseulle flow
